resources.string: Tunnel is enabled. Availability depends on the current network and ADB status.
Tunnel is disabled. Enable it on the phone before connecting.
No allowed network address is available. Allow a network on the phone and share again.

On your computer, replace YOUR_KEY with your SSH private key path and USER with your SSH username. Its public key must already be allowed on the phone. Run the SSH command first, keep it open, then run adb connect in another terminal. The ADB forwarding target is always 127.0.0.1:5555. Local phone addresses may require the same network or routing; mobile NAT can prevent access.

Verify this server fingerprint through a trusted channel before trusting it. Pin the public key in the computer’s known_hosts as [PHONE_ADDRESS]:19191 followed by the public key above. This configuration contains no private keys or passwords. Network addresses can change.

On Android 10 without root: enable USB debugging, connect to a trusted computer, accept its RSA prompt and run adb -d tcpip 5555. Then enable this tunnel. Repeat USB activation after each phone reboot. This also opens the Android ADB port 5555 on the network: use only a trusted network. The app cannot firewall that port without root. Run adb usb from the connected computer to close network ADB when finished. Android RSA authorization and SSH keys remain required.
Keep USB debugging for trusted computers

Root keeps USB debugging enabled and prevents approved ADB keys from expiring. New computers still require Android RSA confirmation. After reboot, recovery needs root and may need the first unlock. Turning this off restores the previous key timeout and leaves USB debugging as it is.
su was not found. Root is unavailable: it may be disabled, hidden from this app or not installed. To use SSH without root, choose Wireless Debugging in ADB mode.
Language, Quick Settings tile and diagnostics
Pair ADB first. Pin the SSH host key through physical USB before WAN use. Reconnect SSH and ADB after a network or debugging-port change. The client target stays 127.0.0.1:5555.
This sends an HTTPS request to api.ipify.org. A public address does not prove incoming access: CGNAT, operator filtering or firewall rules can block it. A VPN address may identify its exit.
Wi-Fi and mobile rules work independently of WireGuard. Saving a rule closes existing SSH sessions. Unknown network identities stay closed.

Network identification requires Location and Phone permissions. For Wi-Fi after reboot, set Location → Allow all the time in app settings. SSID is read, not GPS coordinates. Android Location must also be enabled.
No usable IPv4 / blocked by Android
Exact SSID, including case and spaces. No wildcards. Blocked entries always win; unknown SSIDs stay closed.
PLMN: 5 or 6 digits (MCC + MNC) of the connected operator, including roaming. IMS and VPN are excluded; unknown operators stay closed.
Enter the exact identity: no single current network is identified

The app installs its own root controller and early boot guard. Persistent ADB is independent of SSH. TCP ADB requires verified protection; USB debugging and trusted keys are preserved. SSH runs as the app user.
ADB controller has not been configured
ADB controller configured · tap protection status for a live check
These rules apply to direct TCP ADB, including Wireless Debugging ports. Empty values allow only local SSH forwarding. Unknown Wi-Fi and mobile interfaces are closed. SSH has its own network rules.
Without root: pair this phone on a trusted computer.
Enable Wireless Debugging manually in Android Developer options. If Android turns it off, enable it again. The current connect port is discovered automatically.

Enable Wireless Debugging on Wi-Fi, then Pair device with pairing code. Run adb pair PHONE:PAIR_PORT on a trusted computer. The app discovers the connect port. If Android turns debugging off after a reboot or network change, enable it again in Developer options. Pairing and Android network confirmation remain required.

Enable Wireless Debugging on Wi-Fi, then Pair device with pairing code. Run adb pair PHONE:PAIR_PORT on a trusted computer. The app discovers the connect port. Keep-enabled can restore debugging on allowed Wi-Fi after Android turns it off.

On a trusted computer, run once:

adb shell pm grant name.krot.adbsshtunnel android.permission.WRITE_SECURE_SETTINGS

Then enable this switch and Wireless Debugging. While SSH is enabled in non-root mode, the app restores debugging only on allowed Wi-Fi. Turn this switch off before disabling debugging yourself. Pairing and Android network confirmation remain required.
Keep-enabled is off. The current connect port is still discovered automatically.
Grant the one-time keep-enabled permission from a trusted computer.
Waiting for Wireless Debugging to be enabled on allowed Wi-Fi.
Ready to restore debugging on allowed Wi-Fi while non-root SSH is enabled.
OpenSSH public keys, one per line
Saving closes existing SSH sessions. Private keys stay on your computer.
Keys saved. Existing SSH connections are closed.
Created on first SSH startup. Verify via USB before trusting it.

Use ssh-ed25519 or ssh-rsa public keys without options
VPN is active. The external address may identify its exit; incoming access to this phone requires a separate route.
The interface uses carrier NAT space (100.64.0.0/10). Direct incoming access needs a public IPv4 from the operator or another tunnel.
External and interface addresses match. Operator filtering or a firewall may still block incoming SSH.
The external address differs from Wi-Fi. Incoming WAN access may require router port forwarding; this app does not change the router.
External and interface addresses differ. NAT is present; a public address alone does not provide an incoming mapping.
Incoming SSH reachability must be tested from another network.
SSH exited; enable the tunnel to retry
Tap the big button to turn it on
Tap the big button to turn it off
Tap the red note above to fix it
First add your SSH key in “Networks & keys”
Fix it, then tap the big button again
The pasted text is too large. Paste only public keys.
This RSA key is too short. Use an ed25519 key or RSA with at least 2048 bits.
This key is damaged or incomplete. Copy the whole line again.
The Wi-Fi name is too long (at most 32 bytes)
Could not save the settings. Try again.
The phone lets in only computers whose key it knows. The saved key is missing or damaged.
1. On the computer, open ~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub (or id_rsa.pub).\n2. Copy the whole line — it starts with ssh-ed25519 or ssh-rsa.\n3. Tap the button below, paste the line and save.
To know which Wi-Fi you are on, Android needs location access for this app.
1. Tap the button below.\n2. Allow location and choose \"Allow all the time\".\n3. Come back here.
The phone is not connected to Wi-Fi or mobile Internet, so the tunnel has nothing to work on.
1. Turn on Wi-Fi or mobile Internet.\n2. The tunnel starts by itself as soon as a network appears.
Your rules allow the tunnel only on chosen networks, and the current one is not on the list.
1. Open Networks & keys.\n2. Choose Wi-Fi networks or Mobile operators and allow the current one.\n3. If the network name is unknown, first open Android permissions there.
Without root, the tunnel works through Android Wireless Debugging, and it is off right now.
1. Tap the button below to open Developer options.\n2. Turn on Wireless Debugging and confirm the network.\n3. Come back here.
The tunnel is running, but the phone\'s ADB does not answer yet.

1. Open ADB mode and check the chosen mode.
2. Without root: turn on Wireless Debugging.
3. With root: tap Install / update ADB controller.
4. Then tap Try again.
Android did not tell the app the Wireless Debugging port.
1. In Developer options, turn Wireless Debugging off and on again.\n2. Come back and tap Try again.
Root ADB mode needs root access, and this phone does not have it.
1. Open ADB mode.\n2. Choose Wireless Debugging (no root).\n3. Turn the tunnel on again.
The app could not get a root answer to set up ADB protection.
1. Open ADB mode and tap Install / update ADB controller.\n2. Allow root access when the phone asks.\n3. Tap Try again.
The SSH server stopped or could not open port 19191.
1. Tap Try again.\n2. If it happens again, restart the phone: the port may be busy.
The tunnel stopped with an unexpected message.
1. Tap Try again.\n2. If it repeats, open Technical details and copy them when you ask for help.
